searchText: texted this to someone yesterday.   takeaways:  - i probably shouldn't bother applying for the tv job. fsd is handling the screening of candidates and then presenting names to the tigers. i don't have the experience. he said he'd put me in touch with the right guy but i point blank asked if it's something i should apply for and while he didn't say no, i just got the feeling it's not worth my time.   - he was very pleased with my work from the game i did. i am now on his short list of fill-in guys moving forward.   - gave me a few tips of what he's going to look for when they hire the next radio guy.   - wants me to do more digital content work and said no matter what job i apply for in the bigs, the days of just being a broadcaster are over. said that teams aren't asking guys who have been around forever to do more on that front but the next guy he hires will have to be well versed in digital content and social media. one thing he brought up specifically was podcasting. i don’t know if that will apply to all teams, but it’s useful to know what the tigers will want in the future.   - i wasn't going to bring it up in this convo but he brought up me doing some spring games. i said yes and i'll be there whatever dates you need me for. said the deal last year with the west michigan guy was the team paid travel expenses. i told him the seawolves would pay but even if they did not, i'd pay my own way because exposure is what i need. he’s going to get the dates he needs someone for and circle back with me.   - while i'm in lakeland for spring, he wants me to do some tigers.com stuff with player interviews.   - i don't think he was aware i have a #2 so that was good i told him. i told him you need me for a weekend wherever, i am available and his response was that is good to know you have the availability when we have a need. eri greg gania
